qualification: Coverage and synthetic fixture validation only. No AT runtime/browser/manual/performance result is established here. Later outcomes belong in separate current release evidence; preserve this initial map.
evidence_owner_definition: Task IDs identify exact plan execution responsibilities and target evidence artifacts, not people, permissions or completed assignments.
global_qualifications: All 49 requirement statements and acceptance sentences are copied verbatim from TRD revision2; qualified source budgets, proposed targets and source gaps remain unchanged.

Small/representative/stress are approximate proposed workload targets. Counts distinguish local entries, local relations, bindings, imported and loaded records. Reader admission and canonical loading are separate.
Manual actual macOS VoiceOver/Safari walkthrough and precise versions remain required. Windows screen-reader/browser is added when available; otherwise record untested limitation.
People walkthrough records unfamiliar participants or owner-only availability. Roughly30 seconds is a proposed known-term task target, never a measured/universal guarantee.

Cold readable about2s; warm search p95 <=200ms excluding intentional debounce; warm entry p95 <=250ms; focused25/50 graph about1.5s; selection <=100ms. Actual repeated median/p95 and failures required.

Transaction, source identity/freshness, nonmutation, production bundle/offline/CSP, accessibility, distribution, final cutover and rollback require direct current evidence. Fixture schema passes cannot substitute.
Source mappings distinguish exact observed support, missing designation, partial precedence, stale/unavailable source and unexamined coverage. Do not infer global sequence or absence.
Only exact documented startup/session files and harmless preferences are exempt from final before/after preservation; .sys4ai is not generally exempt.

Fixtures may be installed as test resources by existing source distribution. They must never enter the production asset manifest or HTTP allowlist; that later build does not exist at this fixture checkpoint.

scenario_catalog.title: Neutral/import-only reading
scenario_catalog.description: Only locked core vocabulary; specialized empty local corpus and explicitly unspecialized refusal variant.

scenario_catalog.title: Small canonical corpus
scenario_catalog.description: 50 local entries, 100 local relations, separate binding and imported counts; deterministic structured graph.

scenario_catalog.title: Representative target corpus
scenario_catalog.description: 1000 local entries / 5000 relations; requested workload, with actual canonical load and predicted reader admission reported separately.

scenario_catalog.title: Stress target corpus
scenario_catalog.description: 5000 local entries / 50000 relations, partitioned under unchanged per-file limits; bounded refusal is an acceptable measured outcome, not rendering everything.

scenario_catalog.title: Near reference-admission boundary
scenario_catalog.description: Generate adjacent corpora at 1024 and 1025 distinct owner/binding/reference tuples after measuring imported support; do not change limits.

scenario_catalog.title: Second namespace and same label
scenario_catalog.description: Alignment shares its label across namespaces but retains different definitions, IDs, sources, root identity and future sessions/preferences/routes.

scenario_catalog.title: Exact identity, label, alias and lexical discovery
scenario_catalog.description: Alignment duplicate labels and Orientation aliases have explicit distinctions. FixtureTaskManager tests CamelCase normalization; core Task retains case-sensitive ID.

scenario_catalog.title: Lifecycle/category multi-page selection
scenario_catalog.description: Approved/draft/deprecated and asserted/derived/inferred/external entries, long fields and categories; filters must apply before pagination.

scenario_catalog.title: Lossless long data and consuming/deferred markers
scenario_catalog.description: 5000-CJK-character label, Unicode definition, long qualified edge and 130 exact source references; expected service byte/field limits remain future evidence.

scenario_catalog.title: Directed parallel edges, self-loop, cycle and hub
scenario_catalog.description: Distinct documents/supports predicates between same endpoints, one self-loop, directed cycle, explicit process edges and a high-degree focus.

scenario_catalog.title: Rejected broken canonical inputs
scenario_catalog.description: broken_reference -> dangling_target; duplicate_identity -> duplicate_id; unmodeled_ambiguity -> label_ambiguity; unsupported_property -> unsupported_profile; invalid_qualifier -> invalid_qualifiers.

scenario_catalog.title: Reviewed ordered and unsupported order
scenario_catalog.description: Four exact configured process IDs: numbered ordered text, no designation, partial precedence without numbered order, and selected order whose source can become stale/missing. No inferred global sequence.

scenario_catalog.title: Exact evidence and freshness
scenario_catalog.description: Bounded line/range, unique section, repeated heading excerpt, JSON pointer, full-tuple binding distinction, stale/missing/unchanged-mtime bytes.

scenario_catalog.title: Markup and instruction-like data
scenario_catalog.description: Script/image/javascript-link text is inert source content. No external fetch or instruction execution is authorized.

scenario_catalog.title: Continuation scope and progression protocol
scenario_catalog.description: Generate cursors in ephemeral test memory, bind exact Q separately from normalized Q, filters, limits, IDs, roots, snapshots, service, session and monotonic expiry; tamper/replay errors never represented as observed here.

scenario_catalog.title: Coherence and code-epoch protocol
scenario_catalog.description: Use deterministic barriers around both actual publication families, absent/present lock races, unresolved/retained/superseded journals, source-only mismatch, same-mtime bytes and loaded-helper/schema/asset drift.

scenario_catalog.title: Bootstrap, expiry and local service isolation
scenario_catalog.description: Create credentials only at runtime in memory; test one use, removal from history, same-origin session resume, expiry/service stop, cross-service rejection and safe route retention.

scenario_catalog.title: Registered source and manifested asset denial
scenario_catalog.description: Encoded traversal, absolute/unselected path and symlink/hardlink replacements; future tests use temporary roots and assert safe denial without disclosure.

scenario_catalog.title: Direct forbidden dispatch and safe errors
scenario_catalog.description: Probe exact forbidden operations with protected before/after inventory and fail-on-call hooks; browser omissions alone cannot pass.

scenario_catalog.title: Request/cache/worker limits and cancellation
scenario_catalog.description: Measure exact byte/item/visit/scan/deadline/socket/queue/RSS/lease limits; distinguish lower bounds, unknown totals and local display limits. No unsafe retry or changed caps.

scenario_catalog.title: State/routes/history and stale-response protocol
scenario_catalog.description: Late A after B, same normalized/different exact query, atomic refresh, root-scoped preference reset, bounded history/source/cache and graph cleanup.

scenario_catalog.title: Independent List and renderer failure
scenario_catalog.description: Identical normalized relation IDs/direction/qualifiers/scope/warnings; throwing renderer import and layout timeout retain list, evidence and keyboard actions.

scenario_catalog.title: Actual production build and CSP
scenario_catalog.description: Later installed production assets under denied external network; no dev server or screenshots substitute for real package/HTTP evidence.

scenario_catalog.title: Manual and automated accessibility protocol
scenario_catalog.description: Actual VoiceOver/Safari versions and keyboard/focus/320px/zoom/themes/reduced-motion; Windows screen reader/browser when available, otherwise explicit limitation.

scenario_catalog.title: Complete protected-state comparison
scenario_catalog.description: Ontology, source/config, memory, generated outputs, proposals and receipts plus exact startup artifact exceptions; no blanket .sys4ai exemption.

scenario_catalog.title: Source/Template/root/initializer ownership
scenario_catalog.description: Exact manifest, neutral context, independent root adoption, historical editions and no recursive products. Recipes outside HTTP assets; future bundle must be inspected.

scenario_catalog.title: Agent and rollback preservation
scenario_catalog.description: Independent existing retrieval/publication/recovery/Template checks, separate owner provenance work and code rollback preserving newer knowledge/history.

scenario_catalog.title: Repeated production measurement protocol
scenario_catalog.description: Repeated median/p95, hardware/browser/build, cold/warm/debounce exclusions, limits/memory/first unsupported threshold, source validation separately and compressed bundle baseline.

scenario_catalog.title: Knowledge comprehension walkthrough
scenario_catalog.description: Unfamiliar participant or explicitly owner-only walkthrough; known term target roughly30s, wrong turns/mistaken relation meanings/help/wording without statistical generalization.

scenario_catalog.title: Final production visuals and audit
scenario_catalog.description: Nine actual screens, safe local evidence, final source/build/installed versions and preservation after last changes; no credentials or unsupported pass claim.

scenario_catalog.title: Dependency provenance and independent code
scenario_catalog.description: Exact direct/transitive lock/notices, separate build tool/runtime distinction, no copied Logseq implementation or implicit installs.

requirements.title: Replace the human authoring interface with four reading destinations
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Provide Overview, Terms, Processes, and Map as one reader-oriented application, with no browser authoring, administration, or execution capability.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-01: Launching the human interface shows only reading/exploration destinations and loads no draft, review, publish, inference, query-console, AI-generation, or other authoring modules or controls, including hidden Advanced modes.

The project name and global search remain visible; navigation collapses on smaller screens; theme/help remain secondary controls; raw storage kinds, build actions, readiness matrices, proposal counters, and maintenance actions do not become the reader's main navigation.

requirements.title: Read the selected canonical ontology without creating another authority
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Base reader information on the selected project's canonical ontology, locked imports, and source references through existing read semantics and a thin presentation adapter.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Exact canonical identities, labels, definitions, types, aliases, scope notes, examples/non-examples, lifecycle, fact kind, module/version, source references, and canonical locations retain their meaning in the reader; absent fields do not produce invented content.
The adapter creates no second ontology engine or synchronized authority, publishes no changes, and does not derive authoritative data by parsing generated wiki pages or requiring a wiki rebuild.

requirements.title: Keep status, evidence, meaning, and authority distinct
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Present lifecycle, fact classification, source freshness, and execution authority as separate concepts, with interpretation-relevant warnings visible beside affected information.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-08: An exact-ID lookup of a deprecated entry retains its historical definition, status, and recorded replacement link rather than rewriting history.

AT-09: A draft or inferred record exposed through an explicit permitted filter remains visibly distinct from approved asserted knowledge. Default reading prioritizes approved, explicitly recorded information.

Inferred denotes a selected reasoning process's conclusion; Source changed denotes an evidence-version mismatch, not proof of falsity. Approval, freshness, and truth do not collapse into a verified badge. Ontology relationships confer no user/agent action authority.

requirements.title: Offer source-backed starting points
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Make Overview a useful starting page with the configured project purpose, search, real starting identities, and an obvious map entry point.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Starting points come from reviewed presentation configuration or a deterministic explicit project record; node degree does not manufacture a hierarchy. If no starting points exist, browsing categories and search remain available without fabricated content.

With no local extension records, imported core vocabulary remains browsable and the absence of local additions is explained; the first screen is neither a management dashboard nor an unfiltered whole-project graph.

requirements.title: Search deterministically without optional AI
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Reuse canonical deterministic ranking for exact identity, preferred label, alias, and lexical definition/scope matches with semantic fallback explicitly disabled for ordinary explorer search.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-02: Searches for a preferred label, alias, exact ID, and words in a definition return deterministic relevant identities and match reasons with `semantic=False`; the existing agent search default/contract is preserved.

Search neither invokes an LLM nor infers synonyms or generates definitions during navigation. Exact/lexical search remains usable when optional richer search, embeddings, RDF/standards, or inference services are unavailable.
requirements.source_verbatim: U02; SRC §§3.3, 5 UX-02, 9.1, 11.3, 24; LIVE retrieval defaults to semantic=True.

requirements.title: Make results and discovery understandable
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Provide compact search results and alphabetical/category browsing using verified canonical types or reviewed presentation mappings, preserving ambiguity and alias identity.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Results show a human label, supported category, short recorded definition excerpt, disambiguating module/project where needed, and a useful non-obvious match explanation without the scoring formula.

AT-03: When two entries share a label or alias, both appear with distinctions and neither is silently selected. An alias match retains the preferred label and canonical identity rather than creating another page/node.

Categories such as All, Terms, Roles, and Skills appear only when supported by the selected project's types/configuration; category membership never uses name-substring guesses. A neutral or specialized project can expose its supported categories without changing shared frontend code.

requirements.title: Filter and page search without losing valid matches
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Apply visibility, category/lifecycle filters, and ranking before response pagination, with stable bounded continuation and honest incomplete results.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-04: Category/lifecycle filtering across a multi-page result set preserves valid later matches. AT-05: Within one snapshot, continuation produces no duplicate or skipped identities.

Less common filters live under one control, active filters are removable chips, and empty results preserve the query and offer Clear filters or alias guidance. A byte-limited empty response is identified as incomplete, not No matching term.

requirements.title: Present faithful readable entries
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Show the canonical name and definition first, then recorded context, readable incoming/outgoing relationships, sources, and optional technical details.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-07: Definition, aliases, scope note, examples, and non-examples appear faithfully when recorded; absent sections are omitted without runtime paraphrase or invented explanations. Technical IDs do not precede the human definition.

View on map, Copy local link, and Copy stable ID are available reading actions; exact ID, kind, type IDs, module version, fact classification, and canonical location remain inspectable under Details without edit/run actions.

requirements.title: Preserve inspectable relationship meaning and direction
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Make each canonical relationship independently readable with its exact identity, endpoints, predicate, qualifiers, lifecycle, fact classification, and evidence.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-13: Distinct predicates between the same endpoints preserve both canonical relationship IDs, meanings, classifications, and evidence; endpoint-pair grouping never discards a relation. Any visual bundle exposes its count and every member.

AT-14: Incoming traversal retains the canonical subject-predicate-object meaning and directed arrow. An inverse phrase requires a reviewed mapping; otherwise the original sentence order is shown. A friendly relatedTo label never becomes depends on or causes.

Selecting a map edge, its label, or textual description opens the precise relationship with definition, qualifiers, sources/freshness, and stable ID. A scoped/conditional relation never appears unconditional because a qualifier is lengthy.

requirements.title: Explain processes only to the extent sources support them
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Provide explanatory process pages whose purpose, applicability, roles, inputs, outputs, related skills/documents, and ordering are supported by selected canonical records or explicitly linked source sections.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-17: A supported process displays only supported fields and sequence. Ordered text appears before any flow diagram; process pages do not execute a workflow.

AT-18: When order is absent, the page states "An ordered description has not been recorded. These are the documented relationships." and shows those relationships and sources. Graph paths, relatedTo edges, dependencies, and left-to-right layout never establish execution order.

Any optional process diagram exposes evidence for its sequence and branches; the first release can satisfy process access using numbered text and the existing map without another graph library or automatic flow generation.

requirements.title: Inspect exact evidence without losing reading context
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Open an entry's or relationship's authorized source in a secondary panel with a readable label, project-relative path, locator, freshness, and bounded content.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-19: The correct selected identity/reference opens its authorized section or bounded excerpt with evidence status. Hashes remain available under Details while the current entry is retained.

If exact section extraction is unreliable, content is clearly labeled as a bounded excerpt or bounded text view rather than the exact cited passage. Opening evidence executes no source instructions and triggers no automatic external fetch.

AT-20: Changed source bytes are revalidated on opening and visibly distinguished from the originally recorded evidence version; safe recorded definitions remain visible with the mismatch warning, and no provenance hash is repaired by the read.

requirements.title: Preserve navigation state through stable identities
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Use exact canonical IDs in routes and preserve useful discovery, reading, and map context through view switching and browser Back/Forward.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Back/Forward restores selected entry, query, filters, and useful map state. Terms/Map switching preserves selected identity. A deliberate node selection creates one history event, while camera movements do not each create one.

Local link copy excludes credentials and clearly depends on the correct live local service; stable-ID copy supports durable reference without presenting an ephemeral loopback URL as a public sharing link. Standard entry links retain expected new-tab and copy-link behavior after authentication where practical.

requirements.title: Keep harmless preferences separate from knowledge
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Support light, dark, and system themes and a simple reset for project-namespaced view preferences without persisting knowledge edits or source bodies in browser storage.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Theme and optional layout/panel preferences remain isolated per selected project; resetting them changes presentation only. Sensitive source bodies remain in memory, and no canonical edit or general administration/settings model is introduced.

requirements.title: Start the map with a bounded focused neighborhood
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Open Map around a selected canonical identity and its direct relationships; without a selection, offer a reviewed starting point or term picker.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Initial map depth is one relationship step. Approximately 25 visible nodes and 50 edges are proposed initial display defaults, subordinate to stricter project, traversal, item, and payload bounds rather than a request to change agent limits.

No whole-project fetch is used for initial layout, a decorative overview count, or a visual search for a starting node. Root agent defaults remain 2 hops/20 results with maximums of 8 hops/100 results and 32,000 UTF-8 bytes; map defaults do not rewrite those contracts.
requirements.source_verbatim: U02; SRC §§8.1, 8.6, 17.3; UX-04, PERF-01; LIVE current retrieval bounds.

requirements.title: Separate map selection, focus, and deliberate expansion
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Provide explicit map actions for selection, focus, bounded expansion, pan, zoom, Fit view, Reset view, and equivalent list access.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-10: Selecting a node highlights it and updates readable details without moving the camera or changing graph focus. AT-11: Focus here deliberately changes the neighborhood, and Back restores the prior useful state.

Show more connections adds supported nodes/edges from another bounded request/page. Dragging empty space pans; visible zoom controls change scale without changing selected data; Fit view fits visible data only; Reset view restores the focused neighborhood and default presentation.
Escape closes a temporary preview with predictable focus. Essential actions do not depend on double-click, hover, dragging, or a context menu.

requirements.title: Keep the visual graph semantically faithful
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Use canonical node and relationship IDs, preserve graph structures and qualifiers, and distinguish asserted relations from other display layers.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-15: Parallel relations, self-loops, cycles, and qualified relations render without semantic merging or infinite expansion. Relation records normally render as edges; predicate records remain inspectable through labels.

Explicit semantic relations form the default layer; type annotations, source associations, document mentions, inferred results, and navigation categories remain distinct and are not converted into canonical assertions. Sources/bindings do not automatically become graph nodes.
Endpoint labels resolve in the same snapshot. Broken references are reported with the underlying ID still inspectable; no invented label makes a broken concept look valid.

requirements.title: Keep map presentation readable and stable
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Use a restrained, stable two-dimensional map whose direction and labels remain understandable and whose layout does not imply unsupported meaning.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Directed edges show direction and human predicate labels; at crowded zoom, selected/adjacent edge labels remain visible and all labels remain available in the list/details. A compact legend and the instruction "Select a term to read it. Use Focus here to explore its connections." explain operation.

Expansion preserves existing positions where practical, places new nodes near their source, performs only bounded layout adjustment, and stops. Selection or a details panel does not restart the entire layout. Reduced motion is honored; no 3D, continuous motion, glow, unexplained importance sizing, physics sliders, or force controls appear.

Graph distance and position are not represented as semantic similarity, causality, chronology, or importance. If layout times out, valid data remains available in a stable fallback arrangement; an explicit Arrange control is optional when needed.

requirements.title: Explain limits without inventing completeness
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Enforce and distinguish server query limits, browser display limits, and filter exclusions, reporting only supported counts and continuation possibilities.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-06: Omission by byte, time, traversal, or item bounds yields visible incomplete coverage, its reason, displayed scope, and a way to narrow/continue rather than an assertion that nothing exists. AT-12: High-degree expansion remains bounded and discloses omitted connections.

An unknown total or existence of further results remains explicitly unknown; More connections are available is used when only that fact is established. Discovered available_results is never relabeled as a whole-graph total without stronger evidence.

A proposed initial cumulative browser ceiling of 100 nodes and 200 edges is evaluated separately from each request's bounds. At its ceiling, focus, fewer connections, filters, or a list remain available rather than unbounded accumulation or browser freezing.

requirements.title: Give the relationship list full map equivalence
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Provide a first-class accessible List view driven by the same normalized relationship data as Map, with equivalent substantive information and navigation.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-16: Map/List switching retains selection, filters, returned scope, relationship IDs, direction, and warnings. List users can open entries, inspect evidence, focus a term, and request more connections with the same semantics.

AT-29: Major reading and exploration tasks can be completed through keyboard and list without canvas, dragging, hover, or double-click. A small control set avoids hundreds of invisible graph controls in tab order; meaningful result/selection changes are announced rather than every layout frame.

requirements.title: Preserve usable context in empty and failure states
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Provide specific, truthful states for absent data, invalid canonical configuration, expired sessions, service failure, and partial rendering without destroying unrelated readable context.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: No recorded relationships is described as "No relationships are recorded in this view", not a global absence claim. Invalid canonical configuration gives a blocking specific read error and never silently falls back to unrelated/stale data.

AT-23: Session expiry or service stop preserves readable context and the desired route, explains reopening/reconnection, and makes no unauthorized process-restart claim. Loading and regional errors preserve other readable content.
AT-34: Renderer failure leaves definitions, equivalent relationship lists, and evidence access usable; recovery neither enables remote computation/services nor hides missing data as an empty graph.

requirements.title: Display one coherent canonical snapshot
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Bind entry, relationship, source-reference, graph, and continuation data to one validated snapshot of the selected ontology inputs.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-21: Changes during navigation/publication reject mixed-version continuations with a specific snapshot-changed response, preserve the route/screen, and offer Refresh knowledge. Refresh replaces entry, relationships, and graph coherently and discards incompatible cursors and expansions.

Snapshot identity derives from selected input versions rather than a timestamp alone. Materialization uses existing publication/transaction coordination or verified before/after digests with bounded retries; unstable inputs report knowledge being updated instead of a partial graph or misleading empty response.

requirements.title: Cache validated views with bounded lifetime
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Keep caches/indexes tied to selected project/root, validated snapshot, helper/adapter version, and presentation mapping version, without turning cache freshness into authority.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Concurrent reads share a coherent immutable view, incoming/outgoing adjacency supports bounded selection work, memory remains bounded, and retired snapshots are released after active readers finish. Existing publication/recovery coordination is preserved without a conflicting new lock protocol.

Modification times alone never establish evidence-hash equality; source opening revalidates evidence and newly requested current data detects changed inputs. Profiling/optimization retains integrity checks.

requirements.title: Provide compact validated read responses
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Expose bounded versioned reader operations for context, search, exact entry, relationships, neighborhood, and registered source inspection, with explicit coverage and safe failure semantics.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Context returns project/snapshot identity, available categories, and reader capabilities without proposal inventory, authority grants, embedding startup, or broad readiness sweeps. Search uses compact summaries; complete relationships and source bodies are separate bounded reads.

Validated response envelopes identify schema, project, snapshot, requested scope/filters, data, page/continuation, effective limits, coverage, and diagnostics. Completeness applies to the requested scope, not the whole ontology; item, byte, traversal, time, and filter exclusions remain distinguishable; unknown hasMore remains null; any total declares its count scope and exactness.

Unavailable identity, ambiguous label, invalid request, expired session, changed snapshot, stale source, resource limit, and unexpected failure are distinguishable. A graph response carries exact nodes/labels/categories and edges with relation ID, endpoints, predicate, classification, qualifiers, and evidence references.

requirements.title: Validate continuation against its original read scope
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Bind server-validated continuation to project, snapshot, normalized query, filters, direction, sort order, and the last returned stable key.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Changed query/filter begins a new sequence; changed snapshot invalidates continuation; incompatible requests receive a specific rejection rather than resuming another ontology version. Arbitrary client traversal state cannot bypass bounds.
Reader pagination leaves existing agent maximum-result contracts unchanged. More connections means additional independently bounded reads, never uncontrolled recursive scanning.

requirements.title: Reject stale responses and clean up inactive views
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Apply responses only to their current project, snapshot, query, and selection, and stop unused graph resources when navigation changes.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-22: A late entry-A response cannot replace selected entry B; obsolete search cancellation is supported where practical and sequence checks still reject superseded responses even if cancellation loses the race.

Selected identity, graph focus, query/filters, expanded identities, snapshot, source selection, and view preferences remain distinct. Only the application/read layer initiates reads; renderers emit intentions without arbitrary source fetches, ontology execution, or inferred relations.

Graph code/instances load only when needed; selection does not rebuild the graph; leaving the view disposes instances, listeners, timers, and resize observers, and no hidden layout simulation continues. Source excerpts load only on opening.

requirements.title: Make browsing observably non-mutating
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Keep ordinary search, navigation, evidence inspection, and expansion from changing canonical knowledge, configuration, derived products, memory, proposals, or receipts.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Reads never invoke compile, build-wiki, link-memory, profile provisioning, embedding preparation, inference execution, source-hash repair, or optional backend installation. Changed evidence is reported rather than repaired.

AT-33: Before/after hashes and relevant timestamps across the complete browser read workflow establish unchanged ontology, source configuration, memory data/configuration, proposals, publication receipts, and generated products. Only specifically documented startup runtime/session artifacts and harmless preferences are exempt; no broad .sys4ai exemption is allowed.

requirements.title: Keep memory and generated wiki independent
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Keep memory outside first-release browsing and preserve the wiki as an explicit separate derived output.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Opening definitions and following relationships neither queries nor changes memory storage, schema, workflows, or configuration. No historical text is blended into canonical definitions or promoted to current authority.
Missing or stale wiki output does not block canonical browsing or cause an implicit rebuild; existing explicit wiki generation remains available separately.

requirements.title: Run locally with installed production assets
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Use the selected project's Python runtime and a browser for normal launch, serving an explicitly built static frontend and a dedicated read-only service without optional AI or standards prerequisites.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-28: The actual production reader and graph function offline under their real Content Security Policy without remote scripts, CDN downloads, fonts, images, analytics, or cloud logging.

AT-32: Core reads work with optional embedding/RDF/standards/inference services absent; nothing is installed or started implicitly. A reader session does not require enabling the old advanced workbench profile or a Director publication grant.

Normal browsing performs no package installation or build. Missing assets produce a specific incomplete-package error and documented maintenance route. Distributed assets include their dependency lock, build instructions, build identity, and third-party notices through the explicit asset pipeline.

requirements.title: Enforce local reading-session isolation
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Keep the service loopback-only with a server-selected root and equivalent Host, Origin, session, CSRF, and source checks, granting only read access.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-25: Invalid Host/Origin/CSRF/session values and another service's credentials fail without disclosing project data. Browser requests cannot select roots, scan siblings, or access another service/project.

The normal launcher does not bind to 0.0.0.0, permit broad CORS, or substitute an exposed development server. Browser-supplied actor/grant fields cannot supply authoring authority; expiry behavior retains the established authentication posture.

requirements.title: Keep bootstrap credentials out of routes and evidence
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Preserve one-use bootstrap and isolated local session handling while retaining only safe intended navigation state.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Bootstrap is consumed once, removed from the visible URL and retained browser history, and never copied into local links, screenshots, fixtures, logs, Git files, or source references. Session identifiers are isolated by project/service and retain appropriate loopback cookie protections.

Expiry preserves the desired safe route and explains fresh local reopening. An explicitly started convenience launcher may open the browser, but a page does not claim it can restart a stopped Python process without a separately authorized mechanism. Old authoring credentials/tokens are not migrated; fresh reader sessions are created.

requirements.title: Remove browser access to every write dispatcher
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Restrict the explorer dispatcher to session management and defined reads, with no general command, execute, query, function, or authoring dispatch path.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-24: Direct browser requests for draft creation, review decisions, publication, recovery, generation, profile changes, Task mutation, skill/agent execution, or old write endpoints fail and leave protected artifacts unchanged.

Omitted controls, CSS, disabled widgets, and an authoring=false flag are insufficient. The read service cannot invoke authoring operations, while separately permitted CLI/agent implementations and shared trusted-authority helpers remain available under their existing rules.

requirements.title: Constrain source and asset access
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Resolve source access only through selected registered references/snapshots and serve only explicit production bundle assets under safe path, size, and content rules.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-26: Encoded traversal, absolute paths, symlink escapes, and unselected source references are denied; root/allowlist/locator/size/evidence checks remain effective. A source drawer cannot browse arbitrary files.

The actual build manifest or equivalent allowlist rejects unknown/traversing/disallowed-symlink asset paths, serves correct MIME types/security headers, and exposes no repository tree, dependency cache, unnecessary source maps, or package-manager files.

AT-27: HTML, script-like labels/source text, and malicious links render safely without execution. Source excerpts are escaped by default; ontology text is not inserted as raw innerHTML. Production CSP changes are narrow and documented, never broad origins, arbitrary inline scripts, or unsafe-eval as a rendering workaround.

requirements.title: Bound service resources and protect diagnostics
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Apply request-size, execution-time, concurrency, and memory limits while returning safe diagnostic codes and useful short explanations.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Failures do not expose arbitrary Python exception text, credentials, out-of-project absolute paths, or source bodies. Detailed diagnostics remain local with session material redacted.

Browser display, API results, traversal visits, and serialized bytes are independently bounded; existing agent contracts including the inspected 100-visited-node traversal cap and configured byte limit remain intact. Resource exhaustion gives honest bounded degradation rather than unbounded retries or hidden remote computation.

requirements.title: Make ordinary reading accessible
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Target WCAG 2.2 AA using semantic navigation, headings, inputs, buttons, lists, visible unobscured focus, and keyboard alternatives for every essential action.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Search retains a visible labeled input and submit action; autocomplete follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with Arrow Up/Down, Enter, and Escape that dismisses suggestions without erasing the query. Command/Ctrl+K may supplement but never replace visible search.

The page does not use a whole-page application role merely for the graph. Zoom, Fit current view, Focus here, source inspection, and other essential actions work without dragging, hovering, double-clicking, or memorized shortcuts.

Normal text meets 4.5:1 contrast and large text/relevant non-text controls meet their applicable requirements; the WCAG 2.2 AA 24-by-24 CSS-pixel target criterion and its exceptions are assessed correctly. Color is supplemented by labels/icons/line styles, with selection more prominent than decoration.

requirements.title: Preserve predictable focus and feedback
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Manage focus and announcements across sources, menus, navigation, and asynchronous reads without trapping users or discarding context.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Opening a source drawer moves focus to its heading or first meaningful control; closing it restores the evidence trigger. Escape closes temporary menus/drawers and returns focus predictably; route changes do not leave focus in removed components.
Loading preserves current context, errors stay beside the failed region, and updates announce meaningful changes rather than continuous layout frames or whole-page blank flashes.

requirements.title: Support narrow screens, zoom, themes, and reduced motion
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Keep the reader and surrounding controls operable and legible across narrow layouts, substantial zoom, both themes, and reduced-motion settings.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: AT-30: At a 320 CSS-pixel viewport and with substantial browser zoom, menus and text reflow, controls remain usable, and status remains legible. Spatial-diagram exceptions do not excuse non-reflowing surrounding UI.

Narrow navigation becomes a drawer and entry text receives primary space; a phone Map is dedicated with dismissible selected details and a visible List option. Process/source text reads vertically without squeezed parallel columns.

Light and dark themes receive independent checks; reduced motion stops unnecessary animation and settled layouts. System fonts, comfortable line spacing, restrained surfaces, and small consistent spacing support reading; exact visual tuning remains proposed in Decisions.

requirements.title: Keep reusable source and Template distribution explicit
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Author reusable explorer changes in the owning source collection and distribute reviewed assets only through the registered Template update pipeline.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: The future change map identifies affected SKILLS-depo ontology assets, necessary ONTOLOGY-depo contracts/starter content, CLI/docs, bundle manifest/notices, and explicit distribution mappings without restructuring unrelated skills or editing mapped Template files as sources.

Neutral Template output includes required installed production assets and notices, supports its own validated identity/purpose/modules/categories, and has no hard-coded depot labels/IDs. Fixtures remain outside shipped runtime assets; historical verification snapshots and earlier initializer editions remain intact.

requirements.title: Preserve independent project adoption and isolation
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Treat active-root adoption as a separately authorized, inspected file-boundary operation and keep other product projects independent.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Exact source/destination files, local instructions, overwrite boundaries, customizations, affected checks, and final diff are reviewed for root adoption. Registry membership, equal files, or Template distribution does not authorize recursive product updates.

AT-31: Root, neutral Template, and a second explicitly selected fixture with a different namespace and at least one shared label with a different meaning demonstrate isolated routes, caches, preferences, source access, and sessions without hard-coded identity or cross-project leakage.

requirements.title: Define launch, health, and command compatibility honestly
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Provide an explicit reader launch/configuration contract and distinct service identity with documented handling of the retired workbench command.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: A bounded health check distinguishes installed, configured, running, readable, stale, wrong project, and unavailable; it validates the selected context and does not depend on unrelated optional inference/embedding readiness or pretend to be the old authoring service.

The old command either returns a documented deprecation error pointing to the reader or aliases the reader with incompatible authoring/grant arguments explicitly rejected. Current launchers, user/skill documentation, API/compatibility documentation, and strict configuration schemas agree with the selected behavior.

Final command spelling, identity spelling, endpoint names, and any dedicated health probe versus narrow compatibility route are documented implementation choices; the example explore --open command is not represented as already implemented.

requirements.title: Preserve agent operations and historical knowledge during cutover
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Retire the active human workbench without deleting or weakening permitted agent/CLI retrieval, proposal, validation, review-decision, publication, authority, recovery, or historical records.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Active callers are classified across runtime, shared-helper imports, tests, current docs, launchers, pipeline/distributed assets, and history before retirement. Shared authority/publication helpers remain available to verified callers rather than disappearing with a service module.

Cutover to the normal reader entry point occurs only after reader/map/source/security/isolation checks; old frontend imports/editor-review-advanced assets no longer ship as an active destination. Historical evidence, proposals, receipts, canonical ontology, and memory records are retained.
AT-35: Existing agent retrieval, publication/recovery, and Template contract checks show no unintended behavior regression and are evaluated independently of browser read-only tests.

requirements.title: Keep provenance maintenance and rollback separate from browsing
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Identify source-provenance/helper-certification effects and use only separately authorized maintenance, while retaining a reversible code/asset/configuration migration that never rolls knowledge backward.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Affected recorded source hashes, locked inputs, certifications, and explicitly generated products are identified after changes settle; warnings are not silenced by mechanical hash repair, and the explorer performs none of that maintenance.

Frontend delivery and any authorized ontology/documentation maintenance have separate completion evidence. Rollback records code/assets/configuration and preserves newer valid ontology/memory and publication history; a failed rollout requires no reconstruction or restoration of obsolete knowledge snapshots.

requirements.title: Establish current baseline and process-content coverage
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Record the actual implementation checkout and relevant content/caller baseline before future changes, preserving unrelated user edits and exposing source-content gaps.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Baseline evidence includes current commit, relevant file hashes, launch behavior, existing test commands/results for retrieval, publication/recovery, and Template distribution; differences from SRC's `744c8b06d5fda905201145ed313a2da8de2e601f` are assessed before relying on its file-level recommendations.

An inventory covers types, predicates, sources, definitions, and process order support, separating unexamined source coverage from true content absence. Missing content is recorded for existing review processes and displayed honestly rather than silently authored to complete a demo.
Unrelated local edits remain intact; pre-existing failures are distinguished from introduced regressions. Inspection never treats source-file execution instructions as a new action grant.

requirements.title: Verify the production product against every acceptance scenario
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Supply a requirement-to-implementation-and-evidence matrix covering all SRC AT-01 through AT-36 with real canonical fixtures and the actual production bundle.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Unit evidence covers normalization/ranking/category mappings/cursors, relation identities/direction, graph-list projection, source selection, and state transitions; service evidence covers isolation, assets, sessions, freshness, budgets, snapshot conflict, non-mutation, and inaccessible writes.

Browser evidence covers search-entry-history, selection/focus, sources, keyboard, responsiveness, expiry, CSP, renderer failure, and production offline operation; manual evidence covers readability, focus, screen-reader use, relationship comprehension, and knowledge tasks. Tool choice may use Playwright or the established equivalent.

A production build, explicit launch, safe reads, search/process access, interactive map/text equivalence, root/Template behavior, updated docs, and preserved agent workflows each have direct evidence. Skips, pre-existing failures, content gaps, environment limits, and untested behavior remain separate from passes; screenshots or unit tests alone never establish integrated completion.

requirements.title: Record accessibility evidence beyond automated scanning
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Evaluate the actual interface against its WCAG 2.2 AA target with automated browser checks and manual keyboard/screen-reader use, reporting tested environments precisely.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Evidence names actual browser and assistive-technology versions/combinations, including the relevant macOS VoiceOver/Safari walkthrough; a Windows screen-reader/browser combination is added when available, otherwise that limit is reported.
Automated scan results supplement manual knowledge-task and focus checks; component-library selection or a passing scanner never supports an unqualified accessibility/compliance claim.

requirements.title: Measure proposed performance targets honestly
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Benchmark the production explorer on the actual target machine against SRC's qualified initial targets, reporting actual behavior and limits without weakening data integrity.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Proposed benchmark targets retain their conditions: first readable screen within about 2 seconds on cold local launch with installed assets/representative fixture; search applied p95 within 200 milliseconds on a warm snapshot excluding intentional debounce; entry open p95 within 250 milliseconds on warm bounded data; focused graph usable within about 1.5 seconds for roughly 25 nodes/50 edges; loaded-graph selection feedback within 100 milliseconds without full graph recreation.

Additional connections keep the existing view usable with bounded requests, visible progress, and cancellation where practical. Repeated runs report median and p95 with hardware, browser, build, dataset size, payload limits, and cold/warm conditions; no single favorable sample stands for performance.

AT-36: Representative/stress measurements report actual timings, memory use, enforced limits, and graceful degradation. Source-validation latency is profiled separately when dominant, validated immutable input reuse precedes any contract-change proposal, and stale data is never labeled current to meet a target. Compressed bundle size establishes a regression baseline.

requirements.title: Exercise representative and pathological workloads
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Use clearly labeled synthetic small, representative, and stress fixtures that expose semantic, limit, cancellation, and degradation failures.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Suggested scales remain approximate fixture targets: small about 50 entries/100 relationships; representative about 1,000 entries/5,000 relationships; stress about 5,000 entries/50,000 relationships. Existing loader capacity is measured rather than assumed, and stress success means bounded honest behavior rather than rendering everything.

Fixtures include long/duplicate labels, aliases, many sources, distinct predicates on the same endpoints, cycles, self-loops, high-degree hubs, missing references, and large definitions; uniform random graphs alone do not satisfy coverage.

requirements.title: Validate knowledge comprehension with people
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Evaluate whether a person can understand project knowledge through the production interface without learning ontology-management terminology.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: A person unfamiliar with implementation attempts to find/explain a named term, distinguish related terms, interpret relationship endpoints/meaning, visit a neighbor and return, understand a process or its missing ordering, and inspect evidence/freshness. The initial target of finding a known term/definition within roughly 30 seconds without instruction remains a proposed task target, not a universal standard or observed result.

Small exploratory rounds record task completion, wrong turns, mistaken relationship interpretations, requests for help, and participant wording without statistical generalization. If only the owner is available, the same walkthrough is documented and broader validation is explicitly unperformed.
High-impact misunderstandings, including reversed relationships or layout mistaken for causality, are resolved before polish or an unqualified usability claim.

requirements.title: Deliver inspectable evidence and operational documentation
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Provide a focused future implementation handoff with production visuals, launch/build/compatibility instructions, test and measurement evidence, preservation checks, and explicit limitations.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: Actual production screenshots cover Overview, search results, a populated entry, process page, focused map, parallel-edge example, source drawer, incomplete-result state, and narrow-screen view. Static mockups alone do not qualify; private source bodies/session material are removed before any authorized external sharing.

The report records actual commit/build identity, changed-file map, exact commands, test summaries, browser/accessibility coverage, measured limits, protected-file non-mutation, root/Template checks, reversible migration, content gaps, pre-existing failures, skips, and untested environments. Evidence links support claims; credentials, bootstrap links, and unsupported security/accessibility/performance claims are absent.

requirements.title: Implement independently with explicit dependency provenance
requirements.requirement_verbatim: Use Logseq's exploration concepts only as an interaction reference and retain the project's licensing, dependency, and runtime boundaries in the future implementation.
acceptance_criteria_verbatim: No wholesale fork, embedded editor/application, or copied Logseq graph implementation is represented as Sys4AI Apache-licensed code. Any later code reuse needs a specific license review and separate authority; selected dependencies have version checks and required notices.

Python remains the local runtime; no production Node service, second graph/RDF store, GraphQL layer, or independently synchronized browser database is added. A renderer is contained behind a small interface, separate from canonical semantics and read dispatch; a new framework, graph worker, layout extension, or rendering alternative requires a documented need within the existing scope and its lifecycle/security/accessibility/license constraints.

trd_acceptance_source_verbatim.text: AT-01: Launching the human interface shows only reading/exploration destinations and loads no draft, review, publish, inference, query-console, AI-generation, or other authoring modules or controls, including hidden Advanced modes.

AT-02: Searches for a preferred label, alias, exact ID, and words in a definition return deterministic relevant identities and match reasons with `semantic=False`; the existing agent search default/contract is preserved.

AT-03: When two entries share a label or alias, both appear with distinctions and neither is silently selected. An alias match retains the preferred label and canonical identity rather than creating another page/node.
AT-04: Category/lifecycle filtering across a multi-page result set preserves valid later matches. AT-05: Within one snapshot, continuation produces no duplicate or skipped identities.
AT-04: Category/lifecycle filtering across a multi-page result set preserves valid later matches. AT-05: Within one snapshot, continuation produces no duplicate or skipped identities.

AT-06: Omission by byte, time, traversal, or item bounds yields visible incomplete coverage, its reason, displayed scope, and a way to narrow/continue rather than an assertion that nothing exists. AT-12: High-degree expansion remains bounded and discloses omitted connections.

AT-07: Definition, aliases, scope note, examples, and non-examples appear faithfully when recorded; absent sections are omitted without runtime paraphrase or invented explanations. Technical IDs do not precede the human definition.
AT-08: An exact-ID lookup of a deprecated entry retains its historical definition, status, and recorded replacement link rather than rewriting history.

AT-09: A draft or inferred record exposed through an explicit permitted filter remains visibly distinct from approved asserted knowledge. Default reading prioritizes approved, explicitly recorded information.

AT-10: Selecting a node highlights it and updates readable details without moving the camera or changing graph focus. AT-11: Focus here deliberately changes the neighborhood, and Back restores the prior useful state.

AT-10: Selecting a node highlights it and updates readable details without moving the camera or changing graph focus. AT-11: Focus here deliberately changes the neighborhood, and Back restores the prior useful state.

AT-06: Omission by byte, time, traversal, or item bounds yields visible incomplete coverage, its reason, displayed scope, and a way to narrow/continue rather than an assertion that nothing exists. AT-12: High-degree expansion remains bounded and discloses omitted connections.

AT-13: Distinct predicates between the same endpoints preserve both canonical relationship IDs, meanings, classifications, and evidence; endpoint-pair grouping never discards a relation. Any visual bundle exposes its count and every member.

AT-14: Incoming traversal retains the canonical subject-predicate-object meaning and directed arrow. An inverse phrase requires a reviewed mapping; otherwise the original sentence order is shown. A friendly relatedTo label never becomes depends on or causes.

AT-15: Parallel relations, self-loops, cycles, and qualified relations render without semantic merging or infinite expansion. Relation records normally render as edges; predicate records remain inspectable through labels.

AT-16: Map/List switching retains selection, filters, returned scope, relationship IDs, direction, and warnings. List users can open entries, inspect evidence, focus a term, and request more connections with the same semantics.
AT-17: A supported process displays only supported fields and sequence. Ordered text appears before any flow diagram; process pages do not execute a workflow.

AT-18: When order is absent, the page states "An ordered description has not been recorded. These are the documented relationships." and shows those relationships and sources. Graph paths, relatedTo edges, dependencies, and left-to-right layout never establish execution order.
AT-19: The correct selected identity/reference opens its authorized section or bounded excerpt with evidence status. Hashes remain available under Details while the current entry is retained.

AT-20: Changed source bytes are revalidated on opening and visibly distinguished from the originally recorded evidence version; safe recorded definitions remain visible with the mismatch warning, and no provenance hash is repaired by the read.

AT-21: Changes during navigation/publication reject mixed-version continuations with a specific snapshot-changed response, preserve the route/screen, and offer Refresh knowledge. Refresh replaces entry, relationships, and graph coherently and discards incompatible cursors and expansions.

AT-22: A late entry-A response cannot replace selected entry B; obsolete search cancellation is supported where practical and sequence checks still reject superseded responses even if cancellation loses the race.

AT-23: Session expiry or service stop preserves readable context and the desired route, explains reopening/reconnection, and makes no unauthorized process-restart claim. Loading and regional errors preserve other readable content.

AT-24: Direct browser requests for draft creation, review decisions, publication, recovery, generation, profile changes, Task mutation, skill/agent execution, or old write endpoints fail and leave protected artifacts unchanged.

AT-25: Invalid Host/Origin/CSRF/session values and another service's credentials fail without disclosing project data. Browser requests cannot select roots, scan siblings, or access another service/project.

AT-26: Encoded traversal, absolute paths, symlink escapes, and unselected source references are denied; root/allowlist/locator/size/evidence checks remain effective. A source drawer cannot browse arbitrary files.

AT-27: HTML, script-like labels/source text, and malicious links render safely without execution. Source excerpts are escaped by default; ontology text is not inserted as raw innerHTML. Production CSP changes are narrow and documented, never broad origins, arbitrary inline scripts, or unsafe-eval as a rendering workaround.
AT-28: The actual production reader and graph function offline under their real Content Security Policy without remote scripts, CDN downloads, fonts, images, analytics, or cloud logging.

AT-29: Major reading and exploration tasks can be completed through keyboard and list without canvas, dragging, hover, or double-click. A small control set avoids hundreds of invisible graph controls in tab order; meaningful result/selection changes are announced rather than every layout frame.

AT-30: At a 320 CSS-pixel viewport and with substantial browser zoom, menus and text reflow, controls remain usable, and status remains legible. Spatial-diagram exceptions do not excuse non-reflowing surrounding UI.

AT-31: Root, neutral Template, and a second explicitly selected fixture with a different namespace and at least one shared label with a different meaning demonstrate isolated routes, caches, preferences, source access, and sessions without hard-coded identity or cross-project leakage.

AT-32: Core reads work with optional embedding/RDF/standards/inference services absent; nothing is installed or started implicitly. A reader session does not require enabling the old advanced workbench profile or a Director publication grant.

AT-33: Before/after hashes and relevant timestamps across the complete browser read workflow establish unchanged ontology, source configuration, memory data/configuration, proposals, publication receipts, and generated products. Only specifically documented startup runtime/session artifacts and harmless preferences are exempt; no broad .sys4ai exemption is allowed.
AT-34: Renderer failure leaves definitions, equivalent relationship lists, and evidence access usable; recovery neither enables remote computation/services nor hides missing data as an empty graph.
AT-35: Existing agent retrieval, publication/recovery, and Template contract checks show no unintended behavior regression and are evaluated independently of browser read-only tests.

AT-36: Representative/stress measurements report actual timings, memory use, enforced limits, and graceful degradation. Source-validation latency is profiled separately when dominant, validated immutable input reuse precedes any contract-change proposal, and stale data is never labeled current to meet a target. Compressed bundle size establishes a regression baseline.

plan_tasks.title: Freeze implementation baseline and content/caller inventory
acceptance_criteria: The baseline distinguishes pre-existing edits/failures, reader functionality and history; every candidate retirement caller is classified as runtime, shared helper, test, launcher, docs, distribution or historical.
Each process field/order claim has exact source support or an unexamined/absent classification; no canonical content is added to fill a demonstration gap.
The local-file 347-record inventory and complete 412-record loaded inventory retain their different scopes; a canonical process identity is a lead, not evidence of ordered process steps.
verification_steps: Record git rev-parse HEAD, git status --short, selected file SHA256 and stat mtime_ns, interpreter and current explicit launcher behavior without copying session URLs.
Run PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s SKILLS-depo/ontology/tests -p test_query_retrieval.py -v and the same command with test_publication.py; capture actual results.
Run .venv/bin/python tools/template_update.py check and installed core check_ontology.py with exact root; assess any required existing advanced backend before a separate broader test invocation.
risks: Fresh baseline must be captured again if user edits or governing inputs change; inspection/read checks cannot install profiles.

plan_tasks.title: Bind implementation contracts and dependency choices
acceptance_criteria: Contracts define exact request/envelope/error/cursor shapes and numeric request/time/concurrency/cache limits subordinate to canonical limits.

Selected dependency versions, build-only Node version, built-in layout, notices and source provenance are pinned after current primary-source review; any required installation has separate recorded authority.

The contract includes selected-input unresolved-transaction detection, bounded coherent snapshot reads, precise source-reference identity, per-service and per-session cursor scope, independent List normalization and shared state/route ownership.

The change map names source files, generated Template destinations, prospective exact root adoption and current initializer capability compatibility; each preserves its independent authority boundary.
verification_steps: Check current official TypeScript, Cytoscape.js, Vite and dependency license sources for the exact chosen versions.
Review schema compatibility and import boundaries against existing canonical loader/CLI/workbench callers; no new ontology store/engine or source truth is introduced.

Review existing publication intent/receipt/recovery and lock creation semantics, updater exclusions, strict configuration and current initializer resource inventories before approving the proposed contracts.
risks: An incompatible renderer CSP or license finding returns to design review before adopting a workaround; no broad CSP relaxation.
Stable pre/post file digests cannot establish a complete transaction when publication stopped after only some canonical replacements.
Existing dist/build exclusions and initializer v9 resource requirements constrain shipping; do not silently weaken either contract.

plan_tasks.title: Prepare canonical acceptance fixtures and matrix
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover small/representative/stress target shapes, duplicates/aliases, long fields, many sources, parallel predicates, loops/cycles/hubs, broken references and process ordered/unordered examples.
Every TRD requirement and AT item maps to a fixture, code task and evidence owner; generated scale is a proposed workload, never a loader-capacity claim.
verification_steps: Validate fixtures through the existing canonical schema/competency tools; intentionally invalid fixtures have named expected errors.
Inspect runtime distribution inventory to ensure fixture data is not included in the HTTP bundle.

plan_tasks.title: Materialize coherent immutable reader snapshots
acceptance_criteria: Mixed-version inputs yield snapshot_changed/knowledge_updating; entry/relations/graph/cursor output never silently mixes snapshots.
Cache keys include selected root/project, snapshot, helper/adapter and presentation versions; cache memory/concurrency/lifetime are bounded.
Stale evidence does not erase safe canonical definitions and no read creates publication locks, repairs hashes or builds products.

Interrupted multi-file publication with stable bytes is rejected until existing owner state establishes completion or recovery; malformed or unreadable relevant coordination returns a safe bounded diagnostic.
Read-only coordination brackets materialization and covers missing-to-present lock races; ordinary browsing creates no lock, intent, receipt, repaired source hash or generated output.
verification_steps: Inject concurrent selected-file replacement and publication-boundary changes; prove complete view or specific bounded failure with route-refresh semantics.
Test stale source bytes, unchanged-mtime content changes, helper/mapping change and retired snapshot lifecycle; compare protected hashes/timestamps.

Use deterministic barriers with actual publication/recovery helpers on disposable fixtures for active writes, interrupted partial commits with stable digests, missing-lock creation races, relevant versus unrelated transactions and continuous churn. Assert a complete version or specific bounded refusal, never a mixed version.
risks: Stable partial canonical commits are not current coherent snapshots; digest equality alone is insufficient.
Never introduce another coordination store or change writer/publication behavior to make reading convenient.

plan_tasks.title: Adapt deterministic discovery with stable continuation
acceptance_criteria: Exact IDs, labels, aliases and lexical definitions retain deterministic order/reasons; duplicates remain distinct and aliases retain preferred identity.
Category/lifecycle filters apply before paging; one snapshot has no duplicate/skipped IDs and byte-limited empty output is explicitly incomplete.
Changing query, filters, direction, sort, project/root, snapshot, service instance or reading session invalidates a cursor; endpoint bounds never widen agent contracts.
verification_steps: Run fixture cases for AT-02, AT-03, AT-04, AT-05, AT-06, malformed/tampered/expired cursors, exact stable IDs, empty lexical query browsing and unsupported category IDs.
Patch optional semantic/RDF/inference entry points to fail on invocation and verify normal discovery succeeds.
Replay a valid cursor across two concurrent sessions, service restart, expired session and second selected project; only the exact live cursor scope may continue.

plan_tasks.title: Project exact entries and typed neighborhoods
acceptance_criteria: Entry fields are faithful, missing sections are absent, deprecated history/replacement survives exact-ID access, and fact/lifecycle/freshness remain distinct.
Parallel relations retain individual IDs; incoming traversal does not reverse semantic direction; loops/cycles/high-degree data stay bounded with meaningful coverage.
No whole-project browser response is used for layout/start selection; list and map receive the same normalized records and omission semantics.
verification_steps: Run AT-07, AT-08, AT-09, AT-12, AT-13, AT-14, AT-15 data cases; compare every response field to fixture canonical records.
Measure serialized-byte, item, visited-node and time-bound behavior independently, including long qualifier payloads and missing endpoint references.

plan_tasks.title: Implement precise registered source inspection
acceptance_criteria: A source request cannot browse arbitrary paths or another record/project; recorded/current hashes and freshness are distinct.
Exact supported section/line/JSON locators yield precise evidence; unreliable extraction labels bounded excerpt; changed bytes remain visibly stale without repairing provenance.
Text is escaped, sizes are bounded, source bodies stay transient and no external link is fetched automatically.
verification_steps: Run AT-19, AT-20, AT-26, AT-27 with wrong reference IDs, encoded traversal, absolute paths, symlink/hardlink replacement and missing/oversized files.
Check stale opening preserves definition and warns; malicious source instructions remain inert text.

plan_tasks.title: Build read-only HTTP operations and bounded errors
acceptance_criteria: The service imports only reader/transport dependencies and cannot invoke old authoring, query, generic execute or profile/Task/skill mutation operations.
Responses carry schema/project/snapshot/scope/filter/page/effective-limits/coverage/diagnostics, unknown hasMore is null and totals label exact count scope.
Installed/configured/running/readable/stale/wrong-project/unavailable are distinct health facts, independent of optional readiness sweeps.
verification_steps: Run direct HTTP AT-24 write-endpoint probes and assert protected manifests unchanged.

Exercise every invalid/ambiguous/expired/changed/stale/resource/unexpected failure class; ensure short diagnostics contain no raw Python exceptions, source bodies, private session material or out-of-root paths.

plan_tasks.title: Enforce bootstrap and project-isolated sessions
acceptance_criteria: Invalid Host/Origin/CSRF/session and other-service credentials disclose no project data; server fixes root and rejects browser authority/scope fields.
Bootstrap consumes once, leaves visible URL/history before navigation and never appears in copied local links, diagnostics, test fixtures or evidence.
Expiry uses fresh reader sessions and preserves safe desired context; browser never claims it restarts Python.
verification_steps: Run AT-23, AT-25 against simultaneous projects/services, wrong cookie namespaces, reused bootstrap, missing Origin on authenticated POST, forged grants and cross-site navigation.
Inspect retained history, copy targets and redacted service logs; assert no 0.0.0.0 binding or permissive CORS.

plan_tasks.title: Package explicit offline production assets
acceptance_criteria: Installed production assets include build identity, dependency lock and notices in the package; HTTP serves only runtime assets with correct MIME/no-store/nosniff/referrer/CSP protections.
Missing bundle returns incomplete-package error with a maintenance route; no browser launch performs npm/build/install or enables advanced profiles.
Strict explorer configuration is optional-safe-default or explicit validated selected-project configuration; no depot IDs/labels become shared frontend constants.

Manifest, hashed runtime files and notices are included by the unchanged Template discovery rules; dist/build exclusions stay effective. The manifest names runtime assets only, while the lock and build instructions remain package metadata outside HTTP access.
verification_steps: Verify manifest rejects unknown/encoded traversal/symlink assets and excludes repository trees, node_modules, caches, unnecessary maps and package-manager files from HTTP.
Run controlled offline production smoke with external network disabled after an explicitly authorized build; observe CSP failures rather than weakening policy.
Inspect the exact updater-discovered package list and manifest hashes; no requirement depends on excluded dist/build output or a live Node dev server.

plan_tasks.title: Add explicit reader launch and bounded health inspection
acceptance_criteria: The proposed explore --open command starts only the selected reader service and optionally opens a fresh safe bootstrap entry under explicit launch authority.
Health distinguishes installed/configured/running/readable/stale/wrong-project/unavailable without unrelated optional readiness sweeps or startup side effects.
Service identity differs from sys4ai-ontology-workbench; health uses a bounded explicit loopback origin and never accepts a bootstrap URL.
Old authoring CLI behavior is classified and preserved until qualified cutover; no documentation claims the reader can restart a stopped process from a web page.
verification_steps: Run launch/stop/health with optional advanced configuration and runtimes absent, invalid assets/configuration and wrong project origin.
Assert health is bounded and does not provision, read proposal inventory or expose root/source/session details to unauthenticated requests.
Compare help/schema/docs spelling with the exact implemented commands.
risks: Existing advanced-health reports workbench identity and may require a separate legacy assessment path during transition.

plan_tasks.title: Implement shared read client, state and safe route foundations
acceptance_criteria: Pure state transitions preserve distinct identity/focus/query/filter/snapshot/expansion/source/preference fields and reject obsolete response sequences even when cancellation loses a race.
Route codecs encode exact IDs and safe view state; bootstrap/session values and source bodies cannot enter copied links, history state or durable preference storage.
Selection emits one navigation event, camera changes emit none, snapshot conflict retains old coherent context, and explicit refresh discards incompatible cursor/expansion state atomically.
Only the shared read client initiates allowed reads; later screens and renderer consume state and emit intentions. Browser-level Back/Forward and focus integration are assigned to TASK-019.
verification_steps: Run pure route/state tests for IDs, query/filter round trips, late entry-A-after-B responses, cancelled requests, snapshot conflict/refresh and preference reset.
Test bootstrap consumption and safe desired-route restoration with a stubbed session exchange; inspect serialized route/preferences for forbidden secrets or source content.

plan_tasks.title: Implement semantic reader shell and Overview
acceptance_criteria: The first screen exposes only reading destinations and no authoring/advanced modules; no giant graph or management counters are initial navigation.
Overview uses validated project purpose/starting IDs; empty local graph explains imported core vocabulary and offers categories/search.
verification_steps: Inspect production module graph and DOM for AT-01 exclusion compliance.
Exercise a neutral-only fixture and a specialized category mapping without editing shared frontend code.

plan_tasks.title: Implement discoverable accessible search and browsing
acceptance_criteria: Visible labeled search and submit work without shortcuts; autocomplete follows Arrow/Enter/Escape behavior without deleting query.
Results show supported category, preferred label, recorded excerpt and distinctions; lower-frequency filters remain under one control.
All bound/incomplete/empty cases preserve query and offer useful narrow/clear/continue actions without invented totals.
verification_steps: Browser-test AT-02 through AT-06 including multi-page filtering and ambiguity; verify no automatic identity selection.
